mainEntity.name: Does Michigan require a fence around a swimming pool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Michigan has no standalone pool-fence statute, but the residential code points to the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, and Section 305 requires a barrier around any residential pool. Local departments enforce it, and most inspect the barrier before the pool is filled.

mainEntity.name: How tall does a pool fence have to be in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: 48 inches minimum, measured from grade on the side facing away from the pool and held for three feet beyond the barrier. Some Michigan communities require 60 inches — one Oakland County pool builder reports that in Bloomfield Hills, Birmingham, and Beverly Hills — so confirm before ordering posts.

mainEntity.name: Which code edition applies to a Michigan pool right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2015 Michigan Residential Code, which sends pools to the 2015 ISPSC. A 2021 update was filed May 1, 2025, but a July 7, 2025 Court of Claims order paused it, and LARA says the 2015 editions remain in effect. Troy's building department confirms it.

mainEntity.name: Do the horizontal rails on my fence have to face the pool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when the tops of the rails are less than 45 inches apart. In that case the rails must be on the pool side and vertical spacing cannot exceed 1.75 inches. If the rails are 45 inches apart or more, they can face either direction and vertical spacing can go to 4 inches.

mainEntity.name: Does a pool safety cover replace the fence requirement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only a cover rated to ASTM F1346, and only where your building department accepts it. White Lake Township does not accept a powered cover as the barrier for a pool. A standard tarp winter cover is not a safety device and never counts.

mainEntity.name: Can the back wall of my house count as part of the pool barrier?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but every door from the house to the pool area then needs a compliant alarm, self-closing and self-latching hardware, or a rated powered cover. Alarms should meet UL 2017 — audible within seven seconds, 85 decibels at ten feet, deactivation switch at least 54 inches high.

mainEntity.name: Why does my pool gate stop latching in the winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frost heave moves the gate post a quarter inch and the latch misses the strike; Michigan's freeze-thaw cycle lifts and settles shallow footings all winter. Set gate posts deeper, use through-bolted hinges and a gravity latch with travel, and check the gate every few weeks.

mainEntity.name: How much does a pool fence cost in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removable mesh panels run about $15 to $35 per linear foot installed; a 6-foot board-on-board cedar fence runs $55 to $70 per linear foot including tear-out. A 90-foot backyard enclosure in cedar typically lands between $5,000 and $6,500 before gates, staining, and permit.
